content:
We need to find a template that when applied to the given molecule (target) reproduces the forward carbonyl-ene reaction (retro step). The given molecule is the product? The description: "In a carbonyl-ene reaction, an alkene reacts with an allylic hydrogen and a carbonyl group to form a new carbon-carbon bond... The result of the reaction is the formation of a new carbon-carbon bond and a new stereocenter... one of the substituents is going to be a hydroxyl group. Additionally, the reaction involves the change in the order of a C=C bond to a C-C bond, and a C=O bond to a C-O bond. 'ketones' and 'C-C double bonds' are gone, while a 'aliphatic hydroxyl' and a 'five-membered rings' are formed."

Thus forward reaction: starting material has ketone and C=C, product has hydroxyl and five-membered ring. So retrosynthetic step: we need to break product back to precursor with ketone and alkene. The given molecule is product (has OH and five-membered ring). Indeed the SMILES: [CH2:1]=[C:2]([c:3]1... ) ... Wait there is a double bond at start: CH2= C(...). That is an alkene. Also there is a five-membered ring? The part [C@@H:9]1[CH2:10][CH2:11][CH2:12][C@@:13]1([OH:14])... That's a cyclopentane with OH. So product already has both alkene and OH? Hmm carbonyl-ene reaction forms a new C-C bond and OH, but also reduces C=O to C-OH? Actually carbonyl-ene: carbonyl (C=O) reacts with alkene, forming new C-C bond and moving hydrogen to carbonyl oxygen, giving an allylic alcohol (hydroxy). So product has OH and new C-C bond, but retains the alkene? The double bond shifts? Typically ene reaction: C=C + C=O -> new C-C bond, new C-OH, and the double bond moves to adjacent position (forming a new alkene). But description says C=C bond becomes C-C bond (so double bond is lost). So product may have no C=C. But our SMILES shows a C=C at start: [CH2]=[C]... So maybe that is the alkene that will be broken in retrosynthesis (i.e., product still has alkene? hmm). Could be that the product is the starting material for retrosynthesis (i.e., we need to find a template that when applied to product yields precursors). The template should be carbonyl-ene reverse (i.e., break C-OH to C=O and form C=C). So we need a template that matches product (has OH and five-membered ring) and transforms to precursor with ketone and alkene.

Thus we need to search for templates that break aliphatic hydroxyls and five-membered rings, and form ketones and C-C double bonds. Use search_template_catalog_by_criteria with functional_groups_broken = ["aliphatic hydroxyls","five-membered rings"], functional_groups_formed = ["ketones","C-C double bonds"], bonds_broken = ["C-O","C-C"], bonds_formed = ["C=O","C=C"].

But bond format must be like "6-6". We don't know bond types. Maybe we can omit bond criteria and just use functional groups. Let's try search with broken aliphatic hydroxyls and five-membered rings, formed ketones and C-C double bonds.
